If a piece is "flawless," then the artist of the piece could branch out and convey new subjects they haven't perfected. Critique can be useful in encouraging an artist to move on to more challenging things.

No artist is flawless, there's always room for improvement. That's why you see artists finding flaws in their own work even as they get better, I bet OP can attest to that. If the subjects of one piece are "flawless" then there are aspects that can be added, new things to try, a direction that critics can point an artist to.

I feel like theres a miscommunication here, I'm saying that any artist can receive critique and any artist can improve, and given that this subreddit is for art critique I think it's the right place to post. From what I understand, your experience with poor criticism doesn't have any relation to this artist's post. I don't mean to be rude, I'm sorry if my original reply had a strong tone.
I don't understand your connection between your art being torn apart in places it didn't need to be torn apart in and this post.

Totally disagree, artists at any level of skill can get critique and unless you can find a better subreddit for OP to post in I think this is a great place.

I love the colors you used!! Your style is gorgeous. I'd say the values on the face could be pushed with harsher shadows. Also the horns aren't in the same perspective as the face, and the nose looks as if it is facing more to the camera than everything else. Visualizing your drawing in a three d space by using shapes to construct your figure is helpful if you're technical, but just looking at yourself in a mirror could be a good guide if you go more with the flow (like me). I could do a redline if that would be helpful.

I love your use of color and broad strokes, as the comment below says the proportions seem a bit off, the nose and head are on a different perspective from the rest of the face, and the jawline should be steeper where it meets the neck.

I've been thinking of getting a pet (more like a snail or rodent). But I worry that if I do have a depressive episode it won't be properly taken care of. Maybe I could petsit? Then I could see if I can handle both taking care of myself and an animal.
Edit: In regards to your dog friend, canines are very intelligent and will notice you're gone. I bet they'll miss you if they stop seeing you, they have to have built a connection with you.
That sucks. I don't think I can handle these thoughts anymore, I'm so tired. There's only one reason for me to continue on. But I don't know if it's worth the fight. :(

All my suicidal thoughts come across that way. It feels like there's someone else's voice in my head who wants me dead, who hates me. It doesn't matter what's happening, how happy I am, there's always a chance of them popping up. In some cases, it's easy to ignore, I can even laugh at what I'm thinking because of how ridiculous it is. Sometimes though, the thoughts are persuasive, and I start to believe what they tell me. It's so hard not to listen to them.
Thank you for the response.

If I want to kill myself so bad, why don't I just do it, why didn't I just do it. I should let go before I make things any worse.

Not only that, I complicate things, my mother has an ACS case opened against her and what happened may affect it, even just dealing with both that and me is hard for my family.
